the_question: How much could the mask dispute have changed the number the gate acts on?
the_answer: Almost nothing, and that is the case for the statistic rather than a footnote to it.

which_statistic_gates.gated: interquartile spread of subject pixel positions, narrower axis
which_statistic_gates.why_the_dispute_was_about_the_wrong_one: Quartiles are insensitive to a compact cluster at one corner, which is exactly what a fixed annotation is. The extent is defined by the outermost pixel, so a single annotation glyph can set it.

the_plateau_is_necessary_but_not_suffici.what_the_extent_plateau_shows: That the annotation stops pinning the bounding box at 160px of exclusion and the extent reading stops changing.
the_plateau_is_necessary_but_not_suffici.what_it_does_not_show: That the box contains only annotation. The extent stays flat while a wider box removes interior subject pixels that were never on the boundary.
the_plateau_is_necessary_but_not_suffici.what_the_pair_diff_shows_instead: Exactly zero differing pixels through 290px and 360 at 320px rising to thousands by 440px, because two reconstructions of one view differ wherever real geometry sits. The two controls disagree above 290px and the pair diff is right. An earlier version of this sentence said 260px, which understated the certified range by one step of the sweep while the table beside it and widest_certified_overlay_only both read 290.
the_plateau_is_necessary_but_not_suffici.consequence: The pair diff is the load-bearing control. The plateau is corroboration.

a_figure_this_corrects.why_the_old_one_was_too_high: At 440px the box provably contains subject geometry -- the matched pairs differ by thousands of pixels inside it -- so the movement it produced was the spread responding to removed subject content, not to the annotation. Roughly double the true figure.
a_figure_this_corrects.how_it_got_past_me: I took the extent plateau as licence to use the widest box in the sweep, because the extent was flat there. Flat extent means the annotation no longer pins the bounding box; it does not mean the box is empty of subject. The control I needed was the one I already had.

where_the_headline_ratio_sits_among_the_.where_the_headline_figure_sits: The published 26.7x is the second smallest of the nine, not the smallest -- that is 24.5x. Either way it is near the bottom of a 24.5x to 66.2x range, so the conclusion does not depend on a flattering frame.

the_margin_masked_and_unmasked.the_difference_is_the_mask_not_a_disagre: The production gate excludes the same certified overlay region, so 1.74x is the operative margin and 1.77x is the unmasked view of the same thing.

whether_the_ratios_depend_on_the_axis_co.how_to_quote_a_ratio_about_these_frames: Name the numerator axis and the denominator axis. Naming only one is what let this run for three exchanges: a reviewer pinned the extent to the horizontal axis and varied only the spread axis, while this harness moved both together, so each of us was invariant within our own family and neither family was stated. The operative figure is the one the gate reads, extent_narrower_over_spread_narrower. The others are different quantities, not competing measurements of one.
whether_the_ratios_depend_on_the_axis_co.a_claim_of_mine_that_was_scoped_too_broa: I reported a frame as 'convention-invariant' on the strength of four conventions that all moved extent and spread together. It is invariant within that family and not across the reviewer's, where the numerator is pinned. The label claimed more than the control tested, which is the same shape of error as a report that declares its own parameters.
whether_the_ratios_depend_on_the_axis_co.a_hypothesis_of_mine_that_was_refuted: I suggested their figure came from a row misattribution, because it matched this harness's reading of the adjacent frame to within 0.2. They hashed all nine frames against the ones in this PR and found 9 of 9 byte-identical under the same names, which kills it. The coincidence was real and the inference from it was not.
whether_the_ratios_depend_on_the_axis_co.what_this_does_not_claim: That one pairing is correct and another wrong. Both are well-defined quantities over the same pixels. The gate reads one of them, and that is the only reason this harness privileges it.

the_pairing_matrix_isolates_the_remainin.what_agrees: The reviewer's extent-horizontal over spread-vertical column reproduces here exactly on both frames they tabulated, 24.6x and 18.9x.
the_pairing_matrix_isolates_the_remainin.what_does_not: Their extent-horizontal over spread-horizontal column does not: they read 48.5x and undefined where this harness reads 24.6x and 48.3x.
the_pairing_matrix_isolates_the_remainin.what_follows: Since the numerator is shared between their two columns and the vertical spread agrees, neither the extent term nor the vertical spread can be the difference. It is the horizontal quartile spread alone. On one frame this harness's horizontal spread moves 1.97x what theirs does; on the other theirs does not move at all while this one does.
the_pairing_matrix_isolates_the_remainin.why_this_is_the_useful_form: Three exchanges produced two refuted hypotheses, mine about row attribution and theirs about the axis definition. A pairing matrix narrows it to a single term without either of us guessing, and it is a term either harness can print.

why_that_ratio_could_sustain_four_exchan.the_mechanism: The denominator is the relative movement of an interquartile spread under the overlay exclusion. On the disputed frame that movement is two pixels out of 126 at the published tolerance and one pixel at a looser one. Halving a denominator that small doubles the ratio, so the quantity has a one-pixel hinge in it.

the_plateau_around_the_published_conditi.why_it_matters: The published reading is not balanced on the hinge; it sits on a plateau that runs from 0 through 8. That is why it is reproducible, and it is not an argument that the quantity is robust.

but_that_is_not_the_frame_the_headline_c.the_asymmetry: The band table above is for observed_scan_only__overview.png, which is where the dispute happened. The headline ratio comes from candidate_scan_and_surface__topdown.png, which is the widest-swinging of the nine. The argument for banding a frame is that an interval alone does not say whether a reading is reproducible, and by that argument the frame whose number travels is the one that most needs it.
but_that_is_not_the_frame_the_headline_c.the_answer: It sits on a plateau, and a longer one than the disputed frame's: the run containing the published tolerance covers 11 of the 16 swept tolerances against the disputed frame's 5. So the reading the headline quotes is not balanced on the hinge.
but_that_is_not_the_frame_the_headline_c.a_number_this_corrects: This first published the disputed frame's run as 6, contradicting the band table beside it, which gives 0 through 8 at step 2 and so holds five values. The count had been taken over every tolerance sharing the ratio rather than over the run, and 24.58 returns at tolerance 18 after an excursion. Review raised it even though the correction favours the claim: the real contrast is 11 against 5.
but_that_is_not_the_frame_the_headline_c.swing_and_local_stability_are_different_: This is the part worth keeping. The concern was that the widest-swinging frame might be the fragile one, and swing is the ratio of the extremes across the whole sweep, which says nothing about how far the published condition sits from a transition. Here the frame with the widest swing has the longer plateau. Both frames are two steps from their nearest transition, so neither is more locally fragile than the other, and the frame that travels furthest across the sweep is not the one whose published reading is least reproducible. An interval still does not establish reproducibility -- that was the original point -- but neither does a wide interval refute it.

where_the_published_condition_sits_in_ea.candidate_scan_and_surface__topdown.png: published tolerance 6, run 4 through 24: two steps above the lower edge and eighteen below the upper
where_the_published_condition_sits_in_ea.observed_scan_only__overview.png: published tolerance 6, run 0 through 8: the lower edge is the floor of the sweep, and the upper is two steps away

this_is_broader_than_the_frame_it_was_fo.what_that_changes: The reviewer found the hinge on one frame and asked for a stability note. The sweep makes it a property of the ratio rather than a quirk of that frame, which is worse than the note would have implied, so every entry is published with its interval instead.

diagnostic_spread_sensitivity_not_the_pr.why_the_table_is_here_and_not_just_the_s: Mutation testing on this very section found that inflating the summary margin threefold changed the report and broke no test, because the test was reading the claim rather than the readings. That is the same defect a reviewer found in another gate of mine, where the report asserted its own validity. The table lets the test recompute both figures.
diagnostic_spread_sensitivity_not_the_pr.why_the_spread_statistic_has_no_hinge: This diagnostic reads the spread itself, not the relative movement of the spread. An absolute quartile position shifts by a pixel when a pixel crosses the threshold; a ratio whose denominator is that shift moves by a factor of two. The fragile quantity is the diagnostic, and it is fragile because it is a ratio of two small differences. The production gate uses a different background estimator and fixed tolerance and is tested directly elsewhere.

the_dispute_is_now_explained_rather_than.what_the_reviewer_published: 48.5 for the disputed frame and undefined for candidate_surface_only__overview.
the_dispute_is_now_explained_rather_than.what_reproduces_here: At tolerances 24 through 30 this harness reads 48.38 on the disputed frame, and candidate_surface_only__overview is undefined from 22 upward. Their pair is reproducible on these frames at a looser threshold than the one this harness publishes.
the_dispute_is_now_explained_rather_than.so_the_cause_was: An unstated background tolerance acting on a quantity with a one-pixel hinge. Not a misattributed row, not an axis convention, and not the pairing asymmetry that replaced it.
the_dispute_is_now_explained_rather_than.who_found_it: The reviewer, by sweeping their own harness after their first two explanations failed, and against their own published figure. Confirmed here independently on these frames; all five bands match their table.
the_dispute_is_now_explained_rather_than.what_it_cost: Four exchanges, three dead hypotheses -- one of mine about rows, two of theirs about axes and pairing -- for a quantity neither of us had swept.

why_that_ratio_could_sustain_four_exchan.what_this_does_not_claim: That the diagnostic should be removed or that its value at the published tolerance is wrong. It is well defined at a stated condition and it is reproducible there. The claim is narrower: it must be quoted with that condition and with its interval, because a reader recomputing it at a different threshold will otherwise conclude one of the two of us made an arithmetic error.

the_floors_fragility_without_proposing_a.stated_plainly: A reconstruction that moved as much again as the worst movement already measured would put the weakest delivered frame within about 18% of the floor.
the_floors_fragility_without_proposing_a.why_this_is_not_an_argument_for_retuning: It is derived from measured movement, not from the nine frames the threshold was chosen on, so it argues for validating the edge against frames outside these nine rather than for moving the floor on them.

what_this_does_not_establish: That the floor's edge is correct. It establishes that the mask question could not have moved the gate, and that the statistic choice was the right one for a reason that is now measured rather than asserted.

provenance.why_the_anchor_is_stated: Two disagreements about these frames were anchoring conventions rather than data.
